name: Can I remove an interior wall to expand my kitchen layout?

mainEntity.name: Can I remove an interior wall to expand my kitchen layout?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, removing a wall to enlarge a kitchen is a common structural modification, provided proper engineering and load support are in place. If the partition is non-load-bearing, the trade-off is relatively straightforward, involving drywall removal, flooring repairs, and minor electrical relocation. When removing a load-bearing wall, a contractor must install temporary shoring, engineer a replacement support beam (such as an LVL or steel beam), and route electrical, plumbing, or venting lines around the new opening. Before finalizing a plan, homeowners must identify where utilities run within the partition to plan relocation expenses and structural approvals accurately.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, interior walls can be removed to expand your kitchen. Load-bearing walls require temporary shoring, engineered support beams, and utility rerouting.
